Both companies view the PC market as a critical frontier for AI deployment.

comparisons.peer_topic: PC market and AI-driven DRAM demand
comparisons.peer_summary: Next-generation PCs feature AI capabilities and high-performance neural processing chipsets, leading to significantly higher DRAM content, with the company announcing low-power compression-attached memory modules to support AI workloads on PCs.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron identify next-generation AI PCs as a significant driver for memory and hardware requirements. Intel frames AI PCs as part of its broader 'AI continuum' strategy, while Micron specifically notes that next-generation PCs with AI capabilities 'contain high-performance neural processing chipsets' and will have 'significantly more DRAM content.' Micron's focus on the resulting demand for memory components aligns with Intel's strategic emphasis on the hardware ecosystem supporting these AI PC workloads.

sentences.text: We also seek to address every phase of the AI continuum, from the largest, most challenging GenAI and large language models to emerging usages like AI PCs and AI at the edge.
The next generation PCs that have been announced contain high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI.
We expect these devices will have significantly more DRAM content than today's average PC.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA has evolved from pioneering accelerated computing to becoming a full-stack computing infrastructure company offering data-center-scale solutions. Its full-stack includes the CUDA programming model, GPUs, and extensive domain-specific software libraries, SDKs, and APIs.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA describe themselves as full-stack computing infrastructure companies providing end-to-end solutions for AI workloads. Intel states its strategy relies on a 'full spectrum of hardware and software platforms' to support the AI continuum, while NVIDIA defines itself as a 'full-stack computing infrastructure company' whose stack includes foundational CUDA software running on GPUs to accelerate AI model training and inference. Both emphasize the integration of hardware and proprietary software stacks to address complex AI challenges.

sentences.text: We believe we have a full spectrum of hardware and software platforms that offer the open and modular solutions for competitive total cost of ownership and time to value that customers need to win in this era of exponential growth and AI everywhere.
We believe AI represents a generational shift in computing by expanding human abilities and solving the most challenging problems.
NVIDIA is now a full-stack computing infrastructure company with data-center-scale offerings that are reshaping industry.

This deep and broad software stack accelerates the performance and eases the deployment of NVIDIA accelerated computing for computationally intensive workloads such as artificial intelligence, or AI, model training and inference, data analytics, scientific computing, and 3D graphics, with vertical-specific optimizations to address industries ranging from healthcare and telecom to automotive and manufacturing.

comparisons.peer_summary: Mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms with complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device to enable on-demand use cases at lower energy costs.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm view edge devices and personal computing platforms as pivotal for on-device AI. Intel targets 'AI PCs and AI at the edge' as emerging usages to address across the AI continuum, while Qualcomm describes mobile handsets and PCs as 'pervasive AI platforms' where complex generative AI algorithms run on-device. Both companies see the shift toward local processing on client devices as a central part of the AI ecosystem.

sentences.text: We also seek to address every phase of the AI continuum, from the largest, most challenging GenAI and large language models to emerging usages like AI PCs and AI at the edge.

With increased processing power, mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms, with complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device, enabling on-demand and contextual AI use cases at a fraction of the energy required by cloud-based applications.
